name: hyp-38-half-split
comment: SPLIT COUNTERPART of hyp-38-half: every edge that is exactly TWICE another carries a flat 180-degree corner at its midpoint, so one tile's side may be met by two. The {3,8} edge is exactly twice the half-edge, so it carries a flat 180-degree corner at its midpoint and may be met by two neighbours. Eight is even, so the unsplit board already admitted uncut vertices; this one adds the tilings where a full edge is met by two halves instead. Halving a regular tile always produces this ratio — the cut lands on a midpoint, and arc length is additive along a geodesic, in H^2 and on the sphere exactly as in the plane (AL, 2026-08-18). The unsplit board sees only the tilings where every edge is matched whole; this one is a SUPERSET of it, so containment is the check to run. Angles unchanged apart from the flats, which is why the curvature is too: a flat corner adds D/2 to the angle sum and 1 to n, and (n-2)*D/2 grows by exactly the same D/2, so the tile's area is untouched. HALF THE {3,8} TRIANGLE, and a test of the parity argument that explains {3,7}. Eight triangles meet at every {3,8} vertex, so each corner is 45 degrees; an altitude cuts one into a scalene 22.5-90-45 triangle. Chiral, three edge types, the {3,8} edge exactly twice the half-edge. D=16 because 22.5 = 2pi/16; the angles are [1,4,2] and sum to 7 against the 8 a flat triangle would, so the deficit is 1 unit = 22.5 degrees, the tile's area. THE PREDICTION: on {3,7} nothing exists below k=6, because each half-triangle's corner at a vertex is flanked by one FULL edge and one HALF-edge, the two kinds must alternate round the vertex, and 7 is odd — so no {3,7} vertex can be left entirely uncut. Eight is EVEN, so the alternation closes and an uncut {3,8} vertex is allowed. If the argument is right this board has tilings at low k where {3,7} had none, and the alphabet must contain a vertex configuration of eight base corners.
